title: CTS Joshua Intensive — Unit 2: Rahab and the Scarlet Cord

blocks.en: 📖 Joshua Intensive — Unit 2: Rahab and the Scarlet Cord
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Intensivo de Josué — Unidad 2: Rahab y el Cordón Escarlata

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "For the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath." — Joshua 2:11 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque Jehová vuestro Dios es Dios arriba en los cielos y abajo en la tierra." — Josué 2:11 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: Joshua chapter two is a love story written into the middle of a war story. Israel is camped on the eastern bank of the Jordan, the river is at flood stage, the walled city of Jericho stands across the water, and forty years of wilderness wandering have come down to this single hinge moment. Joshua sends two men. The two men do not return with a military intelligence report. They return with a Canaanite woman's confession of faith and a scarlet cord hanging from a window. Before the first soldier ever crosses the river, before the first trumpet ever sounds, before the first stone of Jericho's wall ever falls, God has already begun the conquest of Canaan — and He has begun it inside the heart of a prostitute.
blocks.es_reference: Josué capítulo dos es una historia de amor escrita en medio de una historia de guerra. Israel está acampado en la orilla oriental del Jordán, el río está en pleno desbordamiento, la ciudad amurallada de Jericó se levanta al otro lado del agua, y cuarenta años de peregrinación en el desierto han llegado a este único momento bisagra. Josué envía a dos hombres. Los dos hombres no regresan con un informe de inteligencia militar. Regresan con la confesión de fe de una mujer cananea y un cordón escarlata colgando de una ventana. Antes de que el primer soldado cruce el río, antes de que la primera trompeta suene, antes de que la primera piedra del muro de Jericó caiga, Dios ya ha comenzado la conquista de Canaán — y la ha comenzado dentro del corazón de una prostituta.

blocks.en: This unit walks through Joshua chapter two phrase by phrase. We will see Joshua's wisdom in sending two spies rather than twelve. We will see Rahab's faith and her risk. We will see the covenant the spies cut with her, the scarlet cord that became the sign of her salvation, and the New Testament's astonishing testimony to a Canaanite harlot who was found in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad camina a través de Josué capítulo dos frase por frase. Veremos la sabiduría de Josué al enviar dos espías en lugar de doce. Veremos la fe y el riesgo de Rahab. Veremos el pacto que los espías hicieron con ella, el cordón escarlata que se convirtió en la señal de su salvación, y el asombroso testimonio del Nuevo Testamento de una ramera cananea que fue encontrada en la genealogía de Jesucristo.

blocks.en: I. Two Spies, Not Twelve (Joshua 2:1)
blocks.es_reference: I. Dos espías, no doce (Josué 2:1)

blocks.en: "Now Joshua the son of Nun sent out two men from Acacia Grove to spy secretly, saying, 'Go, view the land, especially Jericho.' So they went, and came to the house of a harlot named Rahab, and lodged there" (Joshua 2:1).
blocks.es_reference: "Josué hijo de Nun envió desde Sitim dos espías secretamente, diciéndoles: Andad, reconoced la tierra, y a Jericó. Y ellos fueron, y entraron en casa de una ramera que se llamaba Rahab, y posaron allí" (Josué 2:1).

blocks.en: Forty years earlier, Moses had sent twelve spies into Canaan. The result was a disaster. Ten of the twelve came back terrified. They told the people the cities were too well fortified, the inhabitants were giants, and Israel could not take the land. Only two — Joshua and Caleb — gave a faithful minority report. The whole nation believed the ten. Israel turned away from the border and wandered the wilderness for forty years until that unbelieving generation died out.
blocks.es_reference: Cuarenta años antes, Moisés había enviado doce espías a Canaán. El resultado fue un desastre. Diez de los doce volvieron aterrados. Le dijeron al pueblo que las ciudades estaban demasiado fortificadas, que los habitantes eran gigantes, y que Israel no podía tomar la tierra. Solo dos — Josué y Caleb — dieron un informe minoritario fiel. La nación entera creyó a los diez. Israel se apartó de la frontera y vagó por el desierto cuarenta años hasta que esa generación incrédula muriera.

blocks.en: Joshua had been one of the twelve. Joshua had stood there and watched what fear-driven reconnaissance can do to a nation. So when Joshua himself becomes the leader, he sends two — not twelve. He picks them carefully. He sends them secretly. And he gives them a focused mission: view the land, especially Jericho. A leader who has tasted the bitterness of his own past failure does not repeat it. Joshua's first tactical decision in chapter two reflects a man who learned what forty years in the wilderness was meant to teach.
blocks.es_reference: Josué había sido uno de los doce. Josué había estado ahí y observado lo que el reconocimiento impulsado por el miedo puede hacerle a una nación. Así que cuando Josué mismo se convierte en el líder, envía dos — no doce. Los escoge cuidadosamente. Los envía secretamente. Y les da una misión enfocada: reconozcan la tierra, y a Jericó. Un líder que ha probado la amargura de su propio fracaso pasado no lo repite. La primera decisión táctica de Josué en el capítulo dos refleja a un hombre que aprendió lo que cuarenta años en el desierto debían enseñarle.

blocks.en: II. The House on the Wall (Joshua 2:1–7)
blocks.es_reference: II. La casa en el muro (Josué 2:1-7)

blocks.en: The two spies enter Jericho and lodge at the house of a woman named Rahab. The text does not soften her profession. She is a harlot. Her house was probably built into the wall of the city itself — verse 15 tells us so — making it a natural stopping place for travelers and a discreet location for spies. Lodging at Rahab's house was not Israel's plan. It was God's providence. The spies do not arrive at the house of a respectable Canaanite. They arrive at the house of a sinful woman whom God had already begun to draw to Himself.
blocks.es_reference: Los dos espías entran en Jericó y se hospedan en la casa de una mujer llamada Rahab. El texto no suaviza su profesión. Es una ramera. Su casa probablemente estaba construida en el muro mismo de la ciudad — el versículo 15 nos lo dice — haciéndola un lugar natural para los viajeros y una ubicación discreta para los espías. Hospedarse en casa de Rahab no era el plan de Israel. Era la providencia de Dios. Los espías no llegan a la casa de una cananea respetable. Llegan a la casa de una mujer pecadora a quien Dios ya había comenzado a atraer hacia sí.

blocks.en: The king of Jericho hears that Israelite spies have entered the city, and his messengers come to Rahab demanding she hand them over. She has already hidden them. "And the woman took the two men and hid them. So she said, 'Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from. And it happened as the gate was being shut, when it was dark, that the men went out. Where the men went I do not know; pursue them quickly, for you may overtake them'" (2:4–5).
blocks.es_reference: El rey de Jericó oye que espías israelitas han entrado en la ciudad, y sus mensajeros vienen a Rahab exigiendo que los entregue. Ella ya los ha escondido. "Pero la mujer había tomado a los dos hombres y los había escondido; y dijo: Es verdad que unos hombres vinieron a mi casa, mas no supe de dónde eran. Y cuando se iba a cerrar la puerta, siendo ya oscuro, esos hombres salieron, y no sé a dónde han ido; seguidlos aprisa, y los alcanzaréis" (2:4-5).

blocks.en: The men are on her roof, hidden under stalks of flax. The king's officers race off in pursuit toward the Jordan, leaving the actual fugitives safely above their heads. Rahab has put her own life in mortal danger to protect two strangers from a nation she has heard about but has never met. The text does not commend her deception morally; it commends her faith. Her actions are the evidence that her heart has already crossed over to Israel's God.
blocks.es_reference: Los hombres están en su azotea, escondidos bajo manojos de lino. Los oficiales del rey salen a toda prisa en persecución hacia el Jordán, dejando a los verdaderos fugitivos a salvo sobre sus propias cabezas. Rahab ha puesto su propia vida en peligro mortal para proteger a dos extraños de una nación de la que ha oído hablar pero que nunca ha conocido. El texto no elogia moralmente su engaño; elogia su fe. Sus actos son la evidencia de que su corazón ya se había pasado al Dios de Israel.

blocks.en: III. Rahab's Confession of Faith (Joshua 2:8–11)
blocks.es_reference: III. La confesión de fe de Rahab (Josué 2:8-11)

blocks.en: The heart of the chapter — and one of the great confessions of faith in the entire Old Testament — comes when Rahab climbs to the roof to speak with the men she has hidden. She does not bargain like a businesswoman. She testifies like a believer.
blocks.es_reference: El corazón del capítulo — y una de las grandes confesiones de fe en todo el Antiguo Testamento — viene cuando Rahab sube al tejado para hablar con los hombres que ha escondido. No regatea como mujer de negocios. Testifica como creyente.

blocks.en: "I know that the Lord has given you the land, that the terror of you has fallen on us, and that all the inhabitants of the land are fainthearted because of you. For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were on the other side of the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed. And as soon as we heard these things, our hearts melted; neither did there remain any more courage in anyone because of you, for the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath" (2:9–11).
blocks.es_reference: "Sé que Jehová os ha dado esta tierra; porque el temor de vosotros ha caído sobre nosotros, y todos los moradores del país ya han desmayado por causa de vosotros. Porque hemos oído que Jehová hizo secar las aguas del Mar Rojo delante de vosotros cuando salisteis de Egipto, y lo que habéis hecho a los dos reyes de los amorreos que estaban al otro lado del Jordán, a Sehón y a Og, a los cuales habéis destruido. Oyendo esto, ha desmayado nuestro corazón; ni ha quedado más aliento en hombre alguno por causa de vosotros, porque Jehová vuestro Dios es Dios arriba en los cielos y abajo en la tierra" (2:9-11).

blocks.en: Notice what Rahab knew, what she had heard, and what she now believed. She knew the Lord had given Israel the land. The conquest had not yet happened, but in her heart it was already settled. She had heard what God had done at the Red Sea forty years earlier and what He had done to Sihon and Og just recently. The news had reached Jericho. The whole city was afraid. But where the king of Jericho responded with fear and locked the gates, Rahab responded with faith and opened her door.
blocks.es_reference: Note lo que Rahab sabía, lo que había oído, y lo que ahora creía. Sabía que el Señor había dado la tierra a Israel. La conquista aún no había sucedido, pero en su corazón ya estaba decidida. Había oído lo que Dios había hecho en el Mar Rojo cuarenta años antes. La noticia había llegado a Jericó. La ciudad entera tenía miedo. Pero donde el rey de Jericó respondió con miedo y cerró las puertas, Rahab respondió con fe y abrió la suya.

blocks.en: The climax of her confession is the climax of the whole chapter: "the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath." A Canaanite prostitute, who had grown up surrounded by altars to Baal and Ashtoreth, declares that the God of Israel is not just one god among many. He is the God — above and below, in heaven and on earth, with no rival anywhere. That confession would not have been out of place on the lips of Moses. It came from the lips of a harlot.
blocks.es_reference: El clímax de su confesión es el clímax del capítulo entero: "Jehová vuestro Dios es Dios arriba en los cielos y abajo en la tierra." Una prostituta cananea, que había crecido rodeada de altares a Baal y Astoret, declara que el Dios de Israel no es solo un dios entre muchos. Es el Dios — arriba y abajo, en cielo y en tierra, sin rival en ninguna parte. Esa confesión no habría estado fuera de lugar en los labios de Moisés. Vino de los labios de una ramera.

blocks.en: Where the king of Jericho responded with fear and locked the gates, Rahab responded with faith and opened her door.
blocks.es_reference: Donde el rey de Jericó respondió con miedo y cerró las puertas, Rahab respondió con fe y abrió la suya.

blocks.en: IV. The Covenant of Mercy (Joshua 2:12–14)
blocks.es_reference: IV. El pacto de misericordia (Josué 2:12-14)

blocks.en: "Now therefore, I beg you, swear to me by the Lord, since I have shown you kindness, that you also will show kindness to my father's house, and give me a true token, and spare my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death" (2:12–13).
blocks.es_reference: "Os ruego pues, ahora, juradme por Jehová, que como he hecho misericordia con vosotros, así la haréis vosotros con la casa de mi padre, de lo cual me daréis una señal segura; y que salvaréis la vida a mi padre y a mi madre, a mis hermanos y hermanas, y a todo lo que es suyo; y que libraréis nuestras vidas de la muerte" (2:12-13).

blocks.en: Rahab's faith is not a private inner experience. It is missionary from the moment of its birth. She immediately asks that her family — father, mother, brothers, sisters, all that they have — be spared with her. She is one woman in one house in one wall in one doomed city, but the moment she comes to faith she begins to evangelize her own household. Faith never stays inside one heart. The first instinct of a saved soul is to bring others into the lifeboat.
blocks.es_reference: La fe de Rahab no es una experiencia interior privada. Es misionera desde el momento de su nacimiento. Inmediatamente pide que su familia — padre, madre, hermanos, hermanas, todo lo que tienen — sea preservada con ella. Es una mujer en una casa en un muro en una ciudad condenada, pero en el momento en que cree comienza a evangelizar a su propia familia. La fe nunca permanece dentro de un solo corazón. El primer instinto de un alma salva es traer a otros al bote salvavidas.

blocks.en: The spies answer with a covenant: "Our lives for yours, if none of you tell this business of ours. And it shall be, when the Lord has given us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with you" (2:14). Two foreign men in a brothel make a blood covenant with a Canaanite prostitute, sworn in the name of the Lord, that her family will be spared in the day of judgment. The grace of God working ahead of the conquest is so wide it scoops up an entire household out of a city marked for destruction.
blocks.es_reference: Los espías responden con un pacto: "Nuestra vida responderá por la vuestra, si no denunciareis este nuestro asunto; y cuando Jehová nos haya dado la tierra, nosotros haremos contigo misericordia y verdad" (2:14). Dos hombres extranjeros en un burdel hacen un pacto de sangre con una prostituta cananea, jurado en el nombre de Jehová, de que su familia será perdonada en el día del juicio. La gracia de Dios que obra antes de la conquista es tan amplia que recoge a una casa entera de una ciudad marcada para la destrucción.

blocks.en: V. The Scarlet Cord (Joshua 2:15–21)
blocks.es_reference: V. El cordón escarlata (Josué 2:15-21)

blocks.en: Rahab lets the spies down by a rope through the window — the same window that was set in the city wall. As they go, the spies give her a sign. "Unless, when we come into the land, you bind this line of scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and unless you bring your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father's household to your own home... it shall be that whoever goes outside the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be on his own head, and we will be guiltless. And whoever is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our head if a hand is laid on him" (2:18–19).
blocks.es_reference: Rahab baja a los espías por una soga a través de la ventana — la misma ventana que estaba puesta en el muro de la ciudad. Mientras se van, los espías le dan una señal. "...si no atares este cordón de grana a la ventana por la cual nos descolgaste, y si no metieres en tu casa a tu padre y a tu madre, a tus hermanos y a toda la familia de tu padre... cualquiera que saliere fuera de las puertas de tu casa a la calle, su sangre será sobre su cabeza, y nosotros sin culpa. Mas cualquiera que estuviere en casa contigo, su sangre será sobre nuestra cabeza, si mano le fuere echada" (2:18-19). "Y ella dijo: Sea así como habéis dicho. Luego los despidió, y se fueron; y ella ató el cordón de grana a la ventana" (2:21).

blocks.en: The mark of her salvation is to be a scarlet cord hanging from her window — visible from the outside, marking her house as the one house in all of Jericho that would not fall when the walls came down. "And she said, 'According to your words, so be it.' And she sent them away, and they departed. And she bound the scarlet cord in the window" (2:21).
blocks.es_reference: La señal de su salvación había de ser un cordón de grana colgado de su ventana — visible desde fuera, señalando su casa como la única casa en todo Jericó que no caería cuando los muros se derrumbaran. "Y ella respondió: Sea así como habéis dicho. Luego los despidió, y se fueron; y ella ató el cordón de grana a la ventana" (2:21).

blocks.en: A scarlet cord, hung from a window, marking a doomed house as a saved house. The Old Testament has another scarlet sign, hundreds of years earlier — the blood of the Passover lamb on the doorposts of Israel in Egypt. And the New Testament has a third scarlet sign, hundreds of years later — the blood of the Lamb of God on the wood of the cross. Three scarlet marks. One pattern. Behold the blood, and pass over.
blocks.es_reference: Un cordón escarlata, colgado de una ventana, marcando una casa condenada como casa salva. El Antiguo Testamento tiene otra señal escarlata, cientos de años antes — la sangre del cordero pascual en los dinteles de Israel en Egipto. Y el Nuevo Testamento tiene una tercera señal escarlata, cientos de años después — la sangre del Cordero de Dios en el madero de la cruz. Tres marcas escarlatas. Un solo patrón. Vea la sangre, y pase de largo.

blocks.en: The scarlet cord in Rahab's window is one of the clearest pictures in the Old Testament of the blood of Christ. The judgment of God was coming on Jericho. Every house in the city stood condemned. But the house under the scarlet sign would be spared. Not because the people inside it were better than the people outside it. Because of the sign. Because of the covenant. Because of the blood.
blocks.es_reference: El cordón escarlata en la ventana de Rahab es uno de los cuadros más claros del Antiguo Testamento de la sangre de Cristo. El juicio de Dios venía sobre Jericó. Cada casa en la ciudad estaba condenada. Pero la casa bajo la señal escarlata sería preservada. No porque la gente dentro fuera mejor que la gente fuera. Por la señal. Por el pacto. Por la sangre.

blocks.en: VI. Rahab in the New Testament — Hebrews, James, Matthew
blocks.es_reference: VI. Rahab en el Nuevo Testamento — Hebreos, Santiago, Mateo

blocks.en: The story of Rahab does not end in Joshua. The New Testament returns to her three times, and each return adds another layer of glory.
blocks.es_reference: La historia de Rahab no termina en Josué. El Nuevo Testamento regresa a ella tres veces, y cada regreso añade otra capa de gloria.

blocks.en: Hebrews 11:31 — "By faith the harlot Rahab did not perish with those who did not believe, when she had received the spies with peace." She is one of only two women named individually in the great roll call of faith in Hebrews 11 — alongside Sarah herself. The Holy Spirit places a Canaanite harlot in the same chapter as Abraham, Moses, and David, and gives her the same word that anchors them all: by faith.
blocks.es_reference: Hebreos 11:31 — "Por la fe Rahab la ramera no pereció juntamente con los desobedientes, habiendo recibido a los espías en paz." Es una de solo dos mujeres nombradas individualmente en el gran llamado de la fe de Hebreos 11 — junto con la misma Sara. El Espíritu Santo coloca a una ramera cananea en el mismo capítulo que Abraham, Moisés, y David, y le da la misma palabra que los ancla a todos: por la fe.

blocks.en: James 2:25 — "Likewise, was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?" James uses Rahab as the proof that genuine faith always shows itself in action. She did not just say she believed — she hid the spies, she sent them out by another way, she risked her life on what she had confessed. Her works were the visible evidence of her invisible faith.
blocks.es_reference: Santiago 2:25 — "Asimismo también Rahab la ramera, ¿no fue justificada por obras, cuando recibió a los mensajeros y los envió por otro camino?" Santiago usa a Rahab como prueba de que la fe genuina siempre se muestra en acción. No solo dijo que creía — escondió a los espías, los envió por otro camino, arriesgó su vida por lo que había confesado. Sus obras fueron la evidencia visible de su fe invisible.

blocks.en: Matthew 1:5 — and this is where the story breaks open. "Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab, Boaz begot Obed by Ruth." The harlot of Jericho married into Israel. Her husband was Salmon — quite possibly one of the two spies she had hidden, though Scripture does not say. Her son was Boaz, who married Ruth the Moabitess. Their son was Obed. Obed's son was Jesse. Jesse's son was David. And from David's line came the Messiah. The Canaanite prostitute is the great-great-grandmother of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Mateo 1:5 — y aquí es donde la historia se abre. "Salmón engendró de Rahab a Booz, y Booz engendró de Rut a Obed." La ramera de Jericó se casó dentro de Israel. Su esposo fue Salmón — posiblemente uno de los dos espías que ella había escondido. Su hijo fue Booz, que se casó con Rut la moabita. Su hijo fue Obed. El hijo de Obed fue Isaí. El hijo de Isaí fue David. Y de la línea de David vino el Mesías. La prostituta cananea es la tatara-tatara-abuela del rey David y antepasada de Jesucristo.

blocks.en: God did not just save Rahab. God grafted her into the bloodline of the Savior. The same scarlet cord that hung from her window foreshadowed the blood of her own descendant, who would die for sinners and prostitutes and Canaanites and outsiders of every kind, fifteen hundred years later, on a hill outside another walled city.
blocks.es_reference: Dios no solo salvó a Rahab. Dios la injertó en el linaje del Salvador. El mismo cordón escarlata que colgaba de su ventana prefiguraba la sangre de su propio descendiente, que moriría por pecadores y prostitutas y cananeos y forasteros de toda clase, mil quinientos años después, en una colina fuera de otra ciudad amurallada.

blocks.en: VII. The Whoever Gospel
blocks.es_reference: VII. El evangelio del "todo aquel"

blocks.en: The story of Rahab is the story of a God who saves the wrong people. By the standards of Israel's law, Rahab was wrong on every count. Wrong nationality — Canaanite. Wrong religion — pagan. Wrong profession — prostitute. Wrong city — Jericho, marked for destruction. Wrong everything. And yet God's grace reached past every wrong category and laid hold of her by faith. The same grace that saved Rahab is the same grace that saves anyone who comes through the same door — by faith, under the scarlet sign.
blocks.es_reference: La historia de Rahab es la historia de un Dios que salva a las personas equivocadas. Por los estándares de la ley de Israel, Rahab estaba equivocada en cada categoría. Nacionalidad equivocada — cananea. Religión equivocada — pagana. Profesión equivocada — prostituta. Ciudad equivocada — Jericó, marcada para destrucción. Equivocada en todo. Y sin embargo la gracia de Dios se extendió más allá de cada categoría equivocada y la asió por la fe.

blocks.en: The gospel of Joshua 2 is the gospel of whoever. Whoever was in the house with Rahab when judgment came was spared. Whoever was outside was lost. The line was not drawn by ethnicity or biography or résumé. The line was drawn by the scarlet cord. Anyone — absolutely anyone — who came under the sign was saved. That is the same gospel Jesus preached: "whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life" (John 3:16). Rahab was a whoever. The thief on the cross was a whoever. So is every reader of these words.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelio de Josué 2 es el evangelio del todo aquel. Cualquiera que estuviera en la casa con Rahab cuando vino el juicio fue preservado. Cualquiera que estuviera fuera fue perdido. La línea no se trazó por etnicidad o biografía o currículum. La línea se trazó por el cordón escarlata. Cualquiera — absolutamente cualquiera — que viniera bajo la señal fue salvo. Ese es el mismo evangelio que Jesús predicó: "todo aquel que en él cree, no se pierda, mas tenga vida eterna" (Juan 3:16).

blocks.en: VIII. Application — Confession That Costs and Confession That Saves
blocks.es_reference: VIII. Aplicación — Confesión que cuesta y confesión que salva

blocks.en: Donald Grey Barnhouse, the great pastor of Tenth Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia, once led a young soldier in the First World War to faith in Christ. The boy came from a wealthy American family, and as the war ended he was about to go home to that pre-war life of parties and privilege. He told Barnhouse he was afraid he would slip back into his old habits — that the love of family and old friends would draw him away from his new faith. Barnhouse counseled him to make public confession of Christ to the first ten people from his old life he met when he got home.
blocks.es_reference: Donald Grey Barnhouse, el gran pastor de la Iglesia Presbiteriana Décima en Filadelfia, una vez guió a un joven soldado en la Primera Guerra Mundial a la fe en Cristo. El muchacho venía de una familia americana adinerada, y al terminar la guerra estaba a punto de regresar a esa vida pre-guerra de fiestas y privilegios. Le dijo a Barnhouse que tenía miedo de deslizarse de regreso a sus viejos hábitos. Barnhouse le aconsejó hacer confesión pública de Cristo a las primeras diez personas de su antigua vida que encontrara al llegar a casa.

blocks.en: The young man stepped off the train at the suburban station and almost immediately ran into a girl he had known socially. She greeted him warmly and asked how he was. He told her, "The greatest thing that could possibly happen to me has happened. I've taken the Lord Jesus Christ as my Savior." Her smile froze. A short while later he ran into an old friend who said they would have great parties now that he was back. He told the friend the same thing. By the time he had told ten people, his old social circle had quietly fallen away from him. He had not lost them. He had been given up by them — separated from them by a confession that simply spoke the truth out loud.
blocks.es_reference: El joven bajó del tren en la estación suburbana y casi inmediatamente se encontró con una muchacha que había conocido socialmente. Ella lo saludó cálidamente y le preguntó cómo estaba. Él le dijo: "Lo más grande que pudiera posiblemente sucederme me ha sucedido. He tomado al Señor Jesucristo como mi Salvador." Su sonrisa se congeló. Un poco después se encontró con un viejo amigo que dijo que tendrían grandes fiestas ahora que había regresado. Le dijo lo mismo. Para cuando había dicho a diez personas, su antiguo círculo social había caído tranquilamente lejos de él. No los había perdido. Ellos lo habían cedido — separados de él por una confesión que simplemente decía la verdad en voz alta.

blocks.en: That is what Rahab did in Jericho. She made a public stand for the God of Israel that risked her life and severed her from everything she had known. The girl who had lived as a Canaanite prostitute became the woman who confessed the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath. The confession cost her everything. The confession saved her family.
blocks.es_reference: Eso es lo que Rahab hizo en Jericó. Hizo una declaración pública por el Dios de Israel que arriesgó su vida y la separó de todo lo que había conocido. La muchacha que había vivido como prostituta cananea llegó a ser la mujer que confesó Jehová vuestro Dios es Dios arriba en los cielos y abajo en la tierra. La confesión le costó todo. La confesión salvó a su familia.

blocks.en: And then there is the photograph story. A young Brazilian girl named Christina ran away from her poor village to the streets of Rio de Janeiro, dreaming of a better life. Her mother Maria followed. Knowing what life her daughter would fall into, Maria went from bar to brothel to hotel, and in each one she taped a photograph of herself onto a mirror or a phone booth. On the back of every photo she wrote one short note. Weeks later, after every dream had become a nightmare, Christina was descending the stairs of a cheap hotel when she saw her mother's picture. She crossed the lobby. She turned the photograph over. The note said: "Whatever you have done, whatever you have become, it doesn't matter. Please come home. I still love you."
blocks.es_reference: Y luego está la historia de la fotografía. Una joven brasileña llamada Cristina huyó de su pobre pueblo a las calles de Río de Janeiro, soñando con una vida mejor. Su madre María la siguió. Sabiendo a qué vida caería su hija, María fue de bar a burdel a hotel, y en cada uno pegó una fotografía de sí misma en un espejo o cabina telefónica. En el reverso de cada foto escribió una nota corta. Semanas después, después de que cada sueño se había convertido en pesadilla, Cristina bajaba las escaleras de un hotel barato cuando vio la imagen de su madre. Cruzó el lobby. Volteó la fotografía. La nota decía: "Hagas lo que hayas hecho, seas lo que te hayas vuelto, no importa. Por favor, ven a casa. Todavía te amo."

blocks.en: That is the gospel preached over the rooftops of Jericho. That is the message hanging from the scarlet cord. Whatever you have done, whatever you have become, it doesn't matter. Come under the sign. Come home. The blood of My Son is enough.
blocks.es_reference: Ese es el evangelio predicado sobre los tejados de Jericó. Ese es el mensaje colgando del cordón escarlata. Hagas lo que hayas hecho, seas lo que te hayas vuelto, no importa. Ven bajo la señal. Ven a casa. La sangre de Mi Hijo es suficiente.

blocks.en: Closing
blocks.es_reference: Cierre

blocks.en: The chapter ends with Rahab back in her house, the scarlet cord tied in her window, her family gathered with her, waiting. Outside, the army of Israel gathers at the Jordan. The walls of Jericho still stand. The day of judgment has not yet come. But the woman in the wall has crossed over already. She has crossed over in her heart. The conquest of Jericho began the day Rahab believed.
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo termina con Rahab de regreso en su casa, el cordón escarlata atado en su ventana, su familia reunida con ella, esperando. Afuera, el ejército de Israel se reúne en el Jordán. Los muros de Jericó aún están en pie. El día del juicio aún no ha llegado. Pero la mujer en el muro ya ha cruzado. Ha cruzado en su corazón. La conquista de Jericó comenzó el día en que Rahab creyó.

blocks.en: And whoever you are — wherever you have been, whatever you have done, however far from home — the same God who hung a scarlet cord on the wall of Jericho is the same God who hung His Son on a cross outside Jerusalem. The sign is up. The door is open. The covenant is sworn. Whoever takes refuge under the scarlet mark of the blood of Christ will not perish in the day the walls come down.
blocks.es_reference: Y quienquiera que usted sea — dondequiera que haya estado, lo que sea que haya hecho, qué tan lejos de casa — el mismo Dios que colgó un cordón escarlata en el muro de Jericó es el mismo Dios que colgó a Su Hijo en una cruz fuera de Jerusalén. La señal está arriba. La puerta está abierta. El pacto está jurado. Todo aquel que tome refugio bajo la marca escarlata de la sangre de Cristo no perecerá en el día en que los muros caigan.

blocks.en: A little boy was once asked if he had found Jesus. He thought about it and said, "Why sir, I didn't know He was lost. But I was, and He found me."
blocks.es_reference: Una vez le preguntaron a un niño pequeño si había encontrado a Jesús. Lo pensó y dijo: "Pero señor, yo no sabía que Él se había perdido. Pero yo sí estaba perdido, y Él me encontró."

blocks.en: Rahab was lost. He found her. He grafted her into the family of His own Son. He wrote her name into the genealogy of the Messiah. And He still does the same today, every time the scarlet cord goes up in another window.
blocks.es_reference: Rahab estaba perdida. Él la encontró. La injertó en la familia de Su propio Hijo. Escribió su nombre en la genealogía del Mesías. Y todavía hace lo mismo hoy, cada vez que el cordón escarlata sube en otra ventana.

sa.prompt: Defend the claim that Joshua's decision to send only two spies (rather than twelve) reflects a leader who has learned from his own past failure. How does this apply to pastoral self-examination?
sa.model: Forty years earlier Moses sent twelve spies, and ten came back with a fear-driven report that the cities were too strong; the nation believed them and wandered the wilderness, while only Joshua and Caleb gave a faithful minority report. Joshua had watched that disaster firsthand. So as leader he sends only two men, chosen carefully and sent secretly, with a focused mission. A leader who has tasted his own past failure does not repeat it.

sa.prompt: Explain Rahab's confession in Joshua 2:9-11 as one of the great Old Testament confessions of faith. What did she know, what had she heard, and what did she now believe? What is the climactic statement?
sa.model: Rahab climbs to the roof and testifies like a believer, not a businesswoman. She says, I know the Lord has given you the land, that the terror of Israel has fallen on Jericho and every heart has melted. She had heard how God dried up the Red Sea and destroyed Sihon and Og. Her confession climaxes: the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath. A Canaanite raised among idols confesses the God of Israel as the only God, with a faith a Moses would own.

sa.prompt: Discuss the scarlet cord as a type of the blood of Christ. Trace the biblical pattern across three scarlet signs: the Passover lamb in Egypt, the cord in Rahab's window, and the cross.
sa.model: Rahab binds a scarlet cord in the window so her house alone will be spared when the walls fall. The mark of her salvation is a scarlet sign visible from outside. The Old Testament has another scarlet sign, the blood of the Passover lamb on Israel's doorposts in Egypt; and the New Testament a third, the blood of the Lamb of God on the cross. Three scarlet marks, one pattern: behold the blood and pass over. The cord is one of the clearest Old Testament pictures of the blood of Christ.

sa.prompt: Apply the principle that faith is missionary from the moment of its birth. How does Rahab's immediate request for her family demonstrate this? What does this teach the new believer?
sa.model: Rahab's faith is missionary from the moment of its birth. The instant she believes, she begs the spies to spare her father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all their household. One woman in one house immediately works to evangelize her own family. Faith never stays inside a single heart; the first instinct of a saved soul is to bring others into the lifeboat. The covenant the spies cut scoops a whole household out of a city marked for destruction.

sa.prompt: Discuss Rahab's appearance in Hebrews 11:31, James 2:25, and Matthew 1:5. What does each New Testament reference add to the meaning of her story, and why is the Matthew genealogy particularly stunning?
sa.model: The New Testament returns to Rahab three times. Hebrews 11:31 places the harlot, by faith, in the great roll call beside Abraham and Moses, one of only two women named. James 2:25 uses her as proof that genuine faith shows itself in works: she hid the spies and risked her life. Matthew 1:5 breaks the story open: Rahab married Salmon, bore Boaz, who fathered Obed, grandfather of David. The Canaanite prostitute became an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

sa.prompt: Defend the 'whoever gospel' embedded in Joshua 2. Why is the line drawn by the scarlet sign rather than by ethnicity, biography, or résumé? Apply to John 3:16.
sa.model: Rahab was wrong on every count, wrong nationality, religion, profession, and city, yet grace reached past every category and laid hold of her by faith. The gospel of Joshua 2 is the gospel of whoever: whoever was inside the house under the scarlet sign was spared; whoever was outside was lost. The line was not drawn by ethnicity or resume but by the scarlet cord. That is the gospel Jesus preached: whoever believes in Him shall not perish, and anyone who comes under the sign is saved.

sa.prompt: Explain the providence in the spies arriving at Rahab's house specifically. Why is it significant that they did not lodge with a respectable Canaanite, but with a sinful woman whom God had already begun to draw to Himself?
sa.model: Lodging at Rahab's house was not Israel's plan; it was God's providence. The spies do not arrive at a respectable Canaanite's door but at the house of a sinful woman built into the city wall, a woman God had already begun to draw to Himself. The same grace that runs ahead of the conquest steers two foreign men to the one home in Jericho where faith was waiting. God's hand, not human strategy, set the harlot's house on their path.

sa.prompt: Discuss the Donald Grey Barnhouse soldier story and its parallel to Rahab. How does public confession both cost the old life and confirm the new?
sa.model: Donald Grey Barnhouse led a young soldier in the First World War to Christ. Afraid he would slip back into his old life when he went home, the boy was told to make public confession of Christ to the first ten people from his old circle he met. Stepping off the train he told a girl, then an old friend, then more, that he had taken Christ as Savior. One by one his old social circle quietly fell away; they gave him up, separated by a confession that simply spoke the truth. That is what Rahab did: a confession that costs the old life and secures the new.

sa.prompt: Defend the claim that 'the conquest of Jericho began the day Rahab believed.' How does this reframe the timing of God's victories?
sa.model: Before the first soldier crossed the Jordan, before a single trumpet sounded, God had already begun the conquest of Canaan inside the heart of a prostitute. Rahab said, I know the Lord has given you the land; the victory had not yet happened, but in her heart it was already settled. She believed before she could see. Faith reckons the promise done before the walls of Jericho ever fall. The grace of God runs ahead of the conquest, claiming a believing heart while the city still sleeps.

sa.prompt: Synthesis: Compose a personal application of Joshua 2 to a person you know who feels disqualified — by past sin, wrong biography, or 'wrong' nationality/background — from the gospel. How does Rahab's story speak to that person?
sa.model: By every human standard Rahab was disqualified, Canaanite, pagan, prostitute, citizen of a doomed city. Yet the gospel of the scarlet cord is for the disqualified: whoever comes under the sign by faith is saved by grace. The line was never drawn by resume; it was drawn by the blood. Rahab proves that no one is too wrong for the whoever gospel. The same grace that scooped a harlot out of Jericho still reaches every disqualified sinner who comes under the sign.
